deferred.note: chronos-services::sessions::list_sessions tolerates a missing table by substring-matching the error message (`err_str.contains("does not exist")`). With the chronos-store fix that branch is now unreachable for the virgin-store case, so the workaround is redundant defence-in-depth. Left in place deliberately (it still guards if the store layer regresses) and recorded here so a future cycle can decide whether to delete it or replace it with a typed match. Out of scope for m9-70 (no behavior change either way).

lens_summary.drift: m9-70 is a two-file B-direct cycle that closes FIND-M9-69-MCP-STORE-ISOLATION (deferred by m9-69) and, while doing so, uncovers and closes a second, lower-severity defect in the same read path. Verification is falsification-first: each of the three fixes was reverted in turn and the corresponding test was observed to fail, which is what makes the guards meaningful rather than decorative. Pre-fix the hermeticity test observed 21 sessions from the developer's real store; post-fix all three crates' unit and integration suites are green (chronos-store 62, chronos-mcp 77 + 49 integration, chronos-services 263) and clippy passes with -D warnings. Production behavior is intentionally unchanged: the production store-opening logic is byte-identical, only relocated into a cfg(not(test)) function. T4-smoke is included because the change is visible through the MCP tool surface (session_list on a fresh store). No new vault CC: local robustness plus test isolation, no new structural drift class.

evidence.falsification: Reverting layer 1+2: test_session_store_list_sessions_skips_unreadable_record and test_list_sessions_on_virgin_store_is_empty both FAIL (1 passed; 2 failed) in chronos-store. Simulating the pre-fix cfg(test) store (reads $HOME): test_default_test_server_does_not_read_the_developer_store FAILS with 'fresh test server must start with an empty store, found 21 session(s)'.
evidence.post_fix: cargo test -p chronos-store --lib => 62 passed; 0 failed. cargo test -p chronos-mcp --lib => 77 passed; 0 failed (including test_list_sessions_after_save, which failed on main). cargo test -p chronos-mcp --tests => 49 passed across 6 integration binaries.

subject.fix: 1) list_sessions skips undeserializable records with a tracing::warn instead of failing the call. 2) Reading a database with no tables yet returns an empty list / false rather than TableDoesNotExist (a genuine fresh-install bug: session_list errored on a brand-new sessions.redb). 3) ChronosServer::new() was split into from_store() plus two open_default_store() variants: production keeps $CHRONOS_DB_PATH/$HOME, cfg(test) returns a fresh in-memory store (a real file is still selectable via CHRONOS_DB_PATH). All 36 ChronosServer::new() sites in the unit suite are now hermetic.
subject.gap: ChronosServer::new() opened $HOME/.local/share/chronos/sessions.redb under cfg(test), so the unit suite wrote to and depended on the developer's real database. That store holds records written by older binaries; bincode is not self-describing, so a stale SessionMetadata layout is undeserializable. list_sessions returned StoreError::Serialization on the first such record, which chronos-services propagated as ListFailed (its only tolerated case was 'does not exist'), turning a foreign record into a hard test failure. Observed pre-fix: a fresh test server listed 21 sessions from the developer's store.

legacy_findings_preserved.summary: Closed. chronos-mcp's unit suite built every server on the developer's real $HOME store, and SessionStore::list_sessions hard-failed on the first stale-schema record, so test_list_sessions_after_save failed deterministically on populated machines. Three layers now fix it: best-effort listing, absent-table-is-empty reads, and a hermetic cfg(test) store. Each layer has a test that fails before its fix.

evidence.falsification: With the absent-table handling reverted, test_list_sessions_on_virgin_store_is_empty FAILS with StoreError::Database(TableDoesNotExist("sessions")).

subject.fix: Both read paths now match redb::TableError::TableDoesNotExist and return the empty answer (Ok(vec![]) / Ok(false)); any other table error still propagates.
subject.gap: $HOME/.local/share/chronos/sessions.redb is created on first start but contains no tables until the first save_session. SessionStore::list_sessions and SessionStore::session_exists opened SESSION_META unconditionally and mapped the redb TableDoesNotExist error into StoreError::Database, which chronos-services only tolerated via a substring match on the error text ('does not exist'). A fresh install therefore answered session_list with an error rather than [].

legacy_findings_preserved.summary: Closed in-cycle. Found by the new hermetic test: reading a session database that has no tables yet returned TableDoesNotExist instead of an empty result, so session_list errored on a brand-new install instead of reporting zero sessions.
